name: Chicken dishes

axes.label: What the place is known for

cells.cooked: Marinated (soy or salt base, garlic, ginger), dusted with flour or starch, fried to order
cells.chicken: Thigh, breast or a mix; also neck, gizzard, cartilage, wings, skin
cells.eaten: As it comes, hot or cold; each shop’s marinade differs
cells.marker: Usa named by the Japan Karaage Association as birthplace of the specialist shop; Nakatsu has 60 or more shops

cells.cooked: Bone-in young chicken simmered in stock from head and bones, in an earthenware pot
cells.chicken: Bone-in pieces, liver, heart, gizzard; carcass for stock
cells.eaten: Soup first, then chicken, then vegetables; zōsui or noodles to finish
cells.marker: Cloudy or clear soup by shop; eaten all year; served at the Hakata Gion Yamakasa

cells.eaten: Vinegared soy with mustard, or ponzu or kabosu
cells.marker: Traced by the farm ministry to Tōyōken in Beppu; eaten across Oita

cells.cooked: Fried; counted as a kind of karaage by the Japan Karaage Association
cells.marker: Two origin stories, no written record
